title: Umar hears Ta-Ha
hookLine: on his way to harm the Prophet ﷺ, Umar reads Ta-Ha at his sister's house and is changed
last: THE STONES WERE NEVER THE POINT.

lines: ON HIS WAY TO END IT.
cards: Mecca, some years after the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ began to preach. A tall, hot-tempered man named Umar ibn al-Khattab walks fast through the streets with a sword.

He's decided the new religion has divided his city long enough, and he's going to end it by killing the man who brought it. On the way, someone stops him: before you fix other people's families, look at your own.
Your sister has become a Muslim.

teach.b: This story comes from Ibn Ishaq's biography of the Prophet, not the Qur'an or Bukhari or Muslim, and the sources tell it with variations, but it's one of the best-loved conversion stories in Muslim memory.
Umar goes to his sister Fatima's house. Inside, she and her husband Sa'id are being taught by a companion named Khabbab, reading from a page. They hear Umar coming and hide the page.
He bursts in: what was that murmuring I heard? He grabs his brother-in-law, and when his sister steps between them, he strikes her and she bleeds. And she says to his face: yes, we're Muslims.
Do what you like. Seeing her blood, Umar is ashamed. He asks for the page.
She says: you're not clean; wash first. He washes. And he reads the opening of Ta-Ha: We did not send down the Qur'an to distress you, but as a reminder.

When he finished, the report says, he said: how beautiful, how noble these words are. Khabbab comes out of hiding. Umar asks where the Prophet is, goes to the house where the Muslims were meeting, and declares his faith.
The man who set out to end the religion became one of its pillars, and later the second caliph.
What changed him? Not an argument, not a miracle, not a threat. His sister's courage, and a page of words read slowly.
This week ran from Dhul-Qarnayn's wall through Zakariyya's secret call, Yahya's gentleness, Ibrahim's peace, love appointed and Ta-Ha's promise, and it ends on a page in a sister's hands.

how: Muslims tell the story of Umar's conversion from the sirah literature as an example of the Qur'an's power to move a hostile heart; many also honor his sister Fatima's courage in the account.

o: the man with a sword whom Ta-Ha's opening changed
the companion who taught the family from a page
the brother-in-law who hid the page from him

games.q: inside the story — tap the pairs.
p: set out to end it; became the second caliph

s: the story of Umar's conversion is told in Sahih al-Bukhari
this version comes from Ibn Ishaq's sirah, with variants in other sources.
his sister told him to wash before touching the page
in Ibn Ishaq's account, she says he must be clean first.
Umar was changed by a debate with the Prophet
in this account he was changed by his sister's courage and reading the page.

games.q: you've just struck your sister, and she's bleeding but unafraid. you see the page they were reading. what does Umar do, as Ibn Ishaq tells it?
o: ask for it, wash as she asks, and read it.
games.why: ashamed, he asks for the page, washes first at her word, reads the opening of Ta-Ha, and says: how beautiful these words are.

practice: Think of a page that once changed you: a verse, a poem, a letter, a line a teacher wrote in the margin. Remember where you were when you first read it, and what shifted.
Then sit with whatever words of it you still carry, and let them do their work again.

wordCard.voice: Umar. The man with a sword who read the opening of Ta-Ha and became one of Islam's pillars. Today's word.
